signals.signal: H1-2026 results (published 04/08/2026): profit after tax EUR 252m, +7% yoy, of which EUR 131m in 2Q2026; ROTE 18.8%; cost-to-income ratio 36% (vs a 2026-2028 target of c.40%); FY2026 net interest income guidance RAISED to c.EUR 750m from c.EUR 720m and cost-to-income guidance improved to <40% from c.40%; interim dividend EUR 0.24 per share (c.EUR 105m, 44% payout, +20% yoy); gross performing loans EUR 11.4bn (+5% ytd), deposits EUR 22.8bn (+3% ytd), total assets EUR 29.1bn, CET1 20.9%. Network disclosed at 30/06/2026: 57 branches in Cyprus of which 1 operates as a cash office; 2,839 staff worldwide.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Group 1H2026 Group Financial Results press release (PDF, p.40 network/staff statement)
signals.implies: Affordability is not the objection. A bank running a 36% cost-income ratio, raising guidance and paying out 44% of half-year profit has free capex for cash-automation and self-service refresh; the sale must be argued on payback and on service continuity, not on cost relief. The 57-branch / 1-cash-office disclosure is the current, authoritative denominator for any Cyprus branch-automation proposal (it supersedes the 56-branch figure carried from Dec-2025).
signals.followup: Ask IR for the technology/branch capex line inside the 2026-2028 plan; the results pack does not break capex out.

signals.signal: Voluntary Staff Exit Plan (VEP): a small-scale, TARGETED VEP was completed during 1H2026 by which 51 full-time employees were approved to leave, at a total cost of EUR 10m, booked mainly as 2Q2026 termination costs (2Q2026 staff costs EUR 57m include c.EUR 9m termination costs). This follows the larger VEP completed at the end of 4Q2025. Total operating expenses EUR 186m, +3% yoy, explicitly attributed to performance-pay accrual and termination cost. Group headcount 2,839 worldwide at 30/06/2026.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus 1H2026 press release - 'Lean operating model' and staff costs sections; 1H2026 results presentation slide 26
signals.implies: Two consecutive VEPs inside nine months, against a branch count that has NOT fallen (57 branches), is the classic precondition for teller cash automation: the same network must be run with fewer people. Printec's cash-automation/recycler line, plus device monitoring and managed services, is the direct answer. 'Targeted' (51 people, EUR 10m, c.EUR 196k per head) signals surgical removal of specific back-office/teller roles rather than a mass exit - so the automation case has to be made role-by-role.
signals.followup: Establish which functions/branches the 51 leavers came from and whether a further VEP tranche is budgeted for 2H2026; ask whether teller headcount specifically was in scope.

signals.signal: Branch reformatting - re-verified live on 27/08/2026 and materially CHANGED since June 2025. The New Branch Model (live since January 2025) now stands at 29 full-service Branches, 12 Lending Units (no teller service), 15 Transaction Branches (teller-only, no lending) and 5 unmanned Digital Branches, plus 17 extended-hours self-service points open to 22:00 behind card-controlled access. In June 2025 the same model was reported by the bank's own network as 40 classic branches, 7 lending units, 7 transaction branches, 6 digital branches and 18 extended-hours points. Net effect over 14 months: full-service branches 40 -> 29 (-11), teller-only Transaction Branches 7 -> 15 (+8), Lending Units 7 -> 12 (+5), Digital Branches 6 -> 5. Bank of Cyprus stated in June 2025 that over 90% of its transactions are already handled electronically.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus - New Branch Model (bank website, EN and GR versions, both read 27/08/2026); prior-state figures from newmoney.gr, 10/06/2025
signals.implies: This is the single most actionable Printec signal for Cyprus. The bank is not closing branches - it is CONVERTING them into single-purpose formats. Eleven ex-full-service sites have been re-cut into teller-only or lending-only formats in 14 months, and each conversion is a physical refit with a cash-handling decision attached: a Transaction Branch is exactly the site profile that justifies teller cash recyclers and assisted self-service, and a Lending Unit that has dropped teller service still needs an ATM and, ideally, a deposit-capable one. Sell the conversion pipeline, not a one-off box order.
signals.likelihood: High - conversions are running now and the trajectory is one-way
signals.followup: Get the remaining conversion schedule (which of the 29 full-service branches are next to become Transaction Branches or Lending Units) and who does the fit-out; the 'branch renovation works' referenced in the 1H2026 ESG section confirms a live refit programme.

signals.signal: Staffless branches quantified from the bank's own machine-location list. The 5 Digital Branches are 'unmanned operating branches' running self-service machines for coin and banknote deposit for authorised legal entities, 7 days a week 08:00-22:00, with ATMs open to all customers. The Cash 360 (Notes & Coins) locations PDF resolves them exactly: branch 0131 Nicosia Mall, 0161 Mall of Cyprus (Latsia), 0368 My Mall (Limassol), 0517 Metropolis Mall (Larnaca), 0601 Kings Avenue Mall (Paphos) - all five listed as 'Unmanned', all five inside shopping malls, all daily 08:00-22:00. The Cash 360 list is still dated 01/12/2025, i.e. no site has been added in nearly nine months.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus - 'Cash 360 (Notes & Coins) Locations' PDF (downloaded and parsed 27/08/2026), and Deposit Machines page
signals.implies: Every real-time cash-acceptance point Bank of Cyprus operates unmanned sits in a shopping mall - a deliberately low-risk, high-footfall pilot estate of five. Two reads for Printec: (1) the format is proven but has NOT been scaled in nine months, so there is an open question the vendor can answer about why (device cost, CIT, monitoring, or cash-in-transit economics), and (2) five unmanned 7-day sites operating to 22:00 cannot be serviced by branch staff - they require remote device monitoring, incident/SLA managed services and cash forecasting, which is a managed-services annuity rather than a hardware sale.
signals.followup: Find out who monitors and first-line-services the five unmanned sites today and when that contract renews; and whether a sixth Digital Branch is planned (a June-2025 press piece cited 6, the bank's own site now says 5 - confirm whether one was closed).

signals.signal: Real-time vs deferred cash acceptance - quantified white space. Parsing the bank's three deposit-machine location PDFs (all downloaded 27/08/2026): Pay-In (BCS) envelope/bag deposit = 32 locations, of which 11 marked Extended Hours; Coin Deposit machines = 30 locations, of which 11 Extended Hours; Cash 360 real-time note-and-coin acceptance = only 5 locations. Pay-In is explicitly deferred credit ('enclosing them in secure envelopes', same-day only if deposited by 11am), whereas Cash 360 counts in real time with the account updated three times within 24 hours. The Pay-In and Coin lists were refreshed 09/06/2026; Cash 360 has not been refreshed since 01/12/2025.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus - Pay In (BCS) Locations and Coin Deposit Machines Locations PDFs (09/06/2026) and Cash 360 Locations PDF (01/12/2025), all parsed locally
signals.implies: 32 business-deposit sites still run on envelope/bag deferred credit while only 5 give real-time value. That gap of c.27 sites is the concrete upgrade pipeline for Printec's cash-automation line - replacing deferred envelope deposit with real-time note-and-coin recycling gives the bank same-day liquidity, removes the back-office count, and gives the merchant customer immediate value, which is the commercial argument that actually moves a corporate cash customer.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no announced programme, but the format gap is documented and the bank is mid-refit
signals.followup: Ask which of the 32 Pay-In sites carry the highest deposit volume - those are the first real-time conversion candidates; and confirm whether the un-refreshed Cash 360 list means the format is paused.

signals.signal: INCUMBENCY RE-VERIFIED, AND THE 'GLORY TCR' PREMISE IS NOT SUPPORTED. Printec Cyprus's own country page (read 27/08/2026 with a desktop user-agent after a 403 on the default fetch) states in its live counters: 128 Teller Cash Recyclers, 152 Self-Service Kiosks, 26,000+ POS terminals supported nationwide, 60+ customers, 17 employees, established 1995. The page carries a named Bank of Cyprus testimonial from Panicos Athanasiades, Manager Consumer Banking Systems & Operations, that the partnership 'has been instrumental in transforming our branches'. The OEM behind the Bank of Cyprus branch estate is SESAMI, not Glory: Sesami's own Bank of Cyprus success story ('The Cash-heavy Path Towards Digitalisation') names Printec as implementation partner and details 43 x XDi-L bag-deposit devices across 35 branches, 34 x CDi-L coin deposit machines and 9 x BCi-L business change machines, rolled out to 35 of 54 branches over three years from 2018. Glory is not named anywhere in the Sesami case study, and targeted English and Greek searches surfaced no Glory-to-Bank-of-Cyprus deployment evidence at all.
signals.source_name: Printec Cyprus country page (printecgroup.com) and Sesami success story 'Bank of Cyprus - The Cash-heavy Path Towards Digitalisation'
signals.implies: Printec is the incumbent branch-automation partner at Bank of Cyprus with a named, quotable reference - so the Cyprus play is defend-and-expand, not displace. Correct the working assumption before any pitch: do NOT plan against a Glory incumbency. The 128 TCRs on the Printec Cyprus counter size the installed base that is now ageing into a refresh window (the Sesami rollout started 2018, so the earliest units are eight years old).
signals.likelihood: High - both vendor sites live and consistent
signals.followup: Confirm with Printec Cyprus how many of the 128 TCRs sit at Bank of Cyprus specifically versus other customers, and the age profile / service-contract renewal dates of the 2018-2021 vintage.

signals.signal: Self-service deposit migration already at scale. Sesami's Bank of Cyprus case study records that by 2024, 82% of deposits were processed through self-service machines, and that Bank of Cyprus 'is currently operating with approximately one-quarter of the teller staff it employed five years ago', with the busiest branches reduced to up to two cashiers. Devices were installed in 35 of 54 branches; CDi-L coin machines are described as so heavily used that 20 units fill two coin bins daily at peak, and some branches needed two XDi-L bag-deposit units.
signals.source_name: Sesami - Bank of Cyprus success story, 'The Cash-heavy Path Towards Digitalisation'
signals.implies: Two selling angles fall straight out of this. First, capacity strain is documented in the vendor's own words - coin bins filling twice daily and branches needing a second bag-deposit unit is an under-capacity signal, i.e. an upsell for higher-capacity or recycling devices. Second, 82% self-service deposit share with a quarter of the old teller headcount means the bank has already proven the ROI internally; the remaining 19 of 54 branches without devices, and the 18% of deposits still over the counter, are the residual addressable volume.
signals.followup: Get the bank to confirm or update the 82% figure for 2026; identify which branches still have no self-service device.

signals.entity: Cyprus banking sector (Bank of Cyprus's home market)
signals.signal: Central Bank of Cyprus H2-2025 payment statistics (PDF pulled and text-extracted locally 27/08/2026): total ATMs in Cyprus fell from 398 at end-H2-2024 to 396 at end-H2-2025, with rural/mountainous installations under a government initiative with the Association of Cyprus Banks more than offset by removals in central locations. c.73% of Cyprus ATMs support contactless vs 38% in the euro area; euro-area ATMs fell 252,249 -> 248,888. ATM numbers in both Cyprus and the euro area are down c.13% over five years. c.EUR 2.6bn was withdrawn from Cyprus ATMs in H2-2025, with the average withdrawal up 27% from EUR 307 (H2-2022) to EUR 390 (H2-2025). CRITICALLY, footnote 11 states that following the two systemic acquisitions completed during 2025, 'further changes in the total number of ATMs in Cyprus may be observed within the coming months as the institutions reassess and rationalise their ATM networks following the integration process.' The CBC also flags that cashback at POS is now the second-preferred cash-withdrawal option in Cyprus per the ECB SPACE 2024 study.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Statistical Release, Payment Statistics: second half of 2025 (PDF)
signals.implies: The regulator has put a dated flag on an imminent, sector-wide ATM rationalisation driven by post-merger integration - that is a decommission/consolidation event, and decommissioning projects are won or lost on migration, logistics and managed-services capability rather than on hardware price. Total addressable Cyprus fleet is c.396 units and shrinking c.13% per five years, so position Printec on refresh, consolidation and monitoring, never on fleet growth. The rising average withdrawal (EUR 390) means fewer, larger transactions - which favours fewer but higher-capacity, deposit-capable machines. The cashback-at-POS finding independently supports the POS/acquiring line.
signals.likelihood: High - regulator explicitly signals rationalisation 'within the coming months'
signals.followup: Track the CBC H1-2026 payment statistics release (due c. Jan-2027) for the post-rationalisation ATM count; meanwhile ask Bank of Cyprus and Eurobank Cyprus directly about fleet plans.

signals.signal: Digital onboarding / eKYC expansion in 1H2026: the bank launched digital business account opening for LEGAL ENTITIES (sight and fixed-term deposit accounts, with the option to order a debit card) so businesses and professionals can transact entirely through digital channels; launched a Digital Car Dealers' Portal giving instant digital quotes at the dealer; extended Joey (banking for minors aged 6-17) to registration from age six and without a device, reaching c.12,900 users by June 2026; launched the Wealthyhood x BoC digital investing platform. Digital Housing Loans reached EUR 33m at 30/06/2026 and total digital loans EUR 225m (from EUR 195m at Dec-2025, +15%). QuickAccounts opened rose from 51,306 to 63,576 (+24% yoy). 517k active digital-channel users, 488k active mobile-app users, 259k active QuickPay users, with one third logging in daily.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus 1H2026 results presentation, slides 24-25, and Interim Financial Report 2026
signals.implies: Digital business account opening is the first time the bank has taken NON-consumer onboarding fully remote, and corporate/legal-entity onboarding is the hardest eKYC problem - UBO identification, corporate document verification, sanctions and PEP screening at entity level. That is precisely where Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC and AML/compliance lines meet. Note that as onboarding moves off-branch, the bank still needs those same businesses to deposit cash somewhere - which reinforces the Cash 360 / real-time acceptance argument rather than undercutting it.
signals.followup: Establish who supplies the identity-verification and corporate-KYC stack behind the new business account opening, and whether it is in-house or vendor.

signals.signal: Fraud, financial-crime and digital-resilience posture in the 1H2026 Interim Financial Report: the Group runs a dedicated Fraud Risk Management unit under Operational Risk whose stated remit includes 'promoting and adopting automated/alert-based systems and controls for the prevention and early detection of external and internal fraud'. It states that ongoing enhancement work has involved 'the further strengthening of external fraud prevention controls and framework, AS A RESULT OF THE CUSTOMERS' ACCELERATED SHIFT TOWARDS DIGITAL CHANNELS'. The report separately names DORA, the EU AI Act and GDPR as active compliance workstreams, describes an AI governance and model-risk framework being built for the AI Act, and identifies Digital Transformation Risk as a key evolving risk with a roadmap covering migration of transactions to digital channels, expansion of fully digital and digitally assisted product sales, embedded banking and 'enhanced self-service solutions', led by a Chief Digital Officer.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Interim Financial Report 2026, sections 4.4.1 Fraud Risk Management, 4.9 Digital Transformation Risk, 4.11 Regulatory Compliance Risk
signals.implies: The bank has written down, in a regulated disclosure, that digital-channel growth is driving fraud-control investment and that it wants automated, alert-based detection - that is a direct, quotable hook for Printec's real-time payment fraud prevention and transaction monitoring products, and for HSM/security around the digital channels. 'Enhanced self-service solutions' appearing inside the board-level digital roadmap is the strategic sentence to quote back when pitching the branch estate. The EU AI Act workstream is a secondary opening for explainable/model-governed monitoring rather than black-box scoring.
signals.likelihood: High - stated commitment in a published interim report
signals.followup: Identify the incumbent fraud/transaction-monitoring vendor and whether the AI Act model-governance work triggers a re-tender of scoring engines.

signals.entity: Bank of Cyprus / JCC Payment Systems
signals.signal: JCC Payment Systems Ltd, described in the 1H2026 press release as 'a leading player in the card processing business and payment solutions, 75% owned by the Bank', contributed net fee and commission income of EUR 15m in 1H2026, +6% yoy, equal to 10% of total Group non-interest income. Separately, the Central Bank of Cyprus notes in its H2-2025 payment statistics that the domestic sector's e-money/remittance/card-acquiring provision is highly concentrated. The Group's net result from insurance operations reached EUR 33m in 1H2026, +35% yoy, helped by the Ethniki Insurance Cyprus acquisition (agreed at EUR 29.5m, completed July 2025, legally merged with EuroLife and General Insurance of Cyprus in December 2025).
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus 1H2026 Group Financial Results press release (JCC and insurance sections)
signals.implies: Bank of Cyprus controls the dominant domestic card-acquiring and processing entity, so any POS/acquiring conversation in Cyprus runs through JCC rather than the bank's retail arm - JCC is the buying centre for POS terminal estates, card processing infrastructure, P2PE and merchant monitoring. Growing JCC fees (+6%) alongside the CBC's finding that cashback at POS is now the second cash-access channel means the merchant terminal estate is doing more work, not less. Printec Cyprus already supports 26,000+ POS terminals nationwide, so map that base against JCC's before pitching.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no announced JCC procurement, but the ownership and growth are confirmed
signals.followup: Open JCC as a distinct account: get its terminal estate size, current terminal vendors, and any Android-POS migration plan.

signals.signal: Control and model-governance failure disclosed for the first time in the 1H2026 Interim Financial Report: during 2026, a review of the Solvency Capital Requirement model at the Group's life insurance subsidiary EuroLife Ltd identified 'a misapplication of specific parameters/components' in the SCR calculation. EuroLife recalculated its Solvency Ratio at 31/03/2026 to 246% versus the 293% previously reported, and at 31/12/2025 to 226% versus 281% previously reported. Regulatory minimums were not breached, the Superintendent of Insurance was informed, and EuroLife has initiated a review of the relevant control and governance framework, undertaking to implement enhancements to model validation, review and monitoring.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Interim Financial Report 2026, B.2.2.3 Capital requirements of subsidiaries
signals.implies: A self-declared model-governance remediation with the regulator informed is a budget-unlocking event. It is adjacent rather than core to Printec's offer, but it strengthens the compliance/model-governance pitch across the Group at exactly the moment the EU AI Act workstream is also live - the Group has just demonstrated to itself that its model validation and monitoring controls needed enhancement. Use it as evidence, not as the pitch.
signals.likelihood: Medium - remediation committed, scope not disclosed
signals.followup: Watch the FY2026 report for the scope of the EuroLife model-validation enhancements and whether it broadens into a Group-wide model risk management programme.

signals.signal: Fleet reconciliation and ATM capability profile. The Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026 (reported 02/07/2026) puts Bank of Cyprus at 2,447 employees, 56 branches and 132 ATMs at the start of 2026, within an eight-member sector of 6,253 staff, 155 branches and 321 ATMs; since 2013 the Cyprus sector has shed 3,020 banking employees, closed 229 branches and lost 102 ATMs. This reconciles cleanly against the bank's own 30/06/2026 disclosure of 57 branches in Cyprus (of which 1 a cash office) and 2,839 staff WORLDWIDE - the ACB figure is Cyprus banking-only, the bank's is group-wide including insurance and overseas subsidiaries, so the two are not in conflict and the branch count has gone UP by one. Note also that the 321 ATMs counted by the ACB across its eight members is well short of the 396 the Central Bank of Cyprus counts island-wide. On capability, the bank's own ATM page states contactless is available across the ENTIRE Bank of Cyprus ATM network, and that ATMs support automatic cash deposit with immediate account credit, cheque deposit in euro with a printed cheque image, bulk cheque deposit of up to 15 cheques per transaction at selected ATMs, and USD/GBP dispense at specific ATMs.
signals.source_name: Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026 as reported by CBN Cyprus Business News, cross-checked against the Bank of Cyprus 1H2026 press release and the bank's own ATM services page
signals.implies: This closes the branch-count reconciliation the previous run left open, and it corrects a tempting misread: Bank of Cyprus is NOT shrinking its branch count. 132 ATMs is the sizing number for any Bank of Cyprus fleet proposal (a third of the island). The gap between the ACB's 321 and the CBC's 396 is c.75 machines outside the eight member banks - independent deployers and non-member institutions - which is separate white space worth mapping. The full-network contactless coverage plus bulk cheque handling means this is a comparatively modern fleet, so lead on deposit-capability and recycling upgrades rather than on basic modernisation.
signals.likelihood: High - both sides of the reconciliation published
signals.followup: Determine how many of the 132 Bank of Cyprus ATMs are deposit-capable versus cash-out only - the bank's public locator has a deposit filter but its data endpoint would not return results to scripted requests (see access issues).

signals.signal: Jinius, the Group's digital B2B/B2C platform, reported at 1H2026: c.1,930 registered companies on the B2B side; c.EUR 1.7bn of money exchanged through the platform in 1H2026 alone (up from EUR 1.1bn in 1H2025, against EUR 2.6bn for FY2025); B2C marketplace gross merchandise value up 160% yoy with product offering up 104% yoy across 16 categories. The B2B proposition explicitly covers electronic invoicing, remittance management, tenders management and ecosystem management, plus the new Car Dealers Portal and embedded banking products such as the Antamivi card rewards scheme.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus 1H2026 results presentation, slides 25 and 58
signals.implies: Bank of Cyprus is building its own merchant-facing rails rather than buying them, and EUR 1.7bn flowing through a bank-owned platform in six months makes Jinius a payments buying centre in its own right. For Printec the openings are on the acceptance and security side rather than the platform side: embedded payment acceptance for the c.1,930 registered companies, POS/Android terminal supply into that merchant base, point-to-point encryption and merchant monitoring. Treat Jinius as an ecosystem to plug into, not a competitor to displace.
signals.likelihood: Medium - growing fast but no disclosed procurement
signals.followup: Establish whether Jinius merchants are acquired through JCC and what terminal estate sits behind them.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-27). Primary-source-first: the entire 04/08/2026 H1-2026 disclosure set - group press release, results presentation and Interim Financial Report - was downloaded and text-extracted locally with pdfminer rather than read through the fetch tool, as were the Central Bank of Cyprus H2-2025 payment statistics and all three Bank of Cyprus deposit-machine location PDFs (which were parsed to produce the 5 / 30 / 32 site counts rather than quoting them). Angles used, deliberately varied from the previous run: (1) the bank's own IR PDF set and announcements index; (2) the bank's public website in BOTH English and Greek, including the New Branch Model page and the ATM services page, plus its raw HTML and its storesMap.js to hunt for a locator data feed; (3) the deposit-machine location PDFs as a machine-countable estate census; (4) the regulator - Central Bank of Cyprus payment statistics, read for the ATM fleet and the rationalisation footnote; (5) the sector body - Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026 via CBN; (6) the VENDOR side, which is the entry point the previous run under-used: Printec's own Cyprus country page and Sesami's Bank of Cyprus success story, both of which carry harder device numbers than any bank source; (7) Greek-language press (newmoney.gr, politis, stockwatch, inbusinessnews) used specifically to date the PRIOR state of the branch model so the change could be measured. BRIEF PREMISE CORRECTED: the task named 'Glory TCR incumbency'. No evidence supports a Glory presence at Bank of Cyprus. Targeted English and Greek searches returned nothing linking Glory to the bank, Glory is absent from Sesami's Bank of Cyprus case study, and the documented chain is Printec as partner with Sesami as OEM. Reported as a correction rather than silently dropped. 'VEP' was read as Voluntary Staff Exit Plan and confirmed in the primary disclosure; the adjacent Verification of Payee (VoP) obligation was also checked and Bank of Cyprus is already compliant with the EU Instant Payments Regulation deadlines of 09/01/2025 (receive) and 09/10/2025 (send, with VoP), so no open deadline sits there. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the bank does not disclose an ATM count in any 2026 IR document - the 132 figure is the Association of Cyprus Banks' and dates to the start of 2026; (b) the deposit-capable share of those 132 ATMs could not be established (see access issues); (c) no capex breakdown for branch or technology investment is published, so no opportunity here can be scoped in euro - hence the Unscoped and band-only sizings; (d) no Cyprus tender or procurement register surfaced any Bank of Cyprus ATM/self-service tender, and Bank of Cyprus is a private company not subject to public procurement publication, so absence of a tender is not evidence of absence of a purchase; (e) the Cash 360 location list has not been refreshed since 01/12/2025, so the five-site figure is nine months old and is reported at its own date rather than as of today. The source catalogue at weekly-intelligence/references/source_catalogue_A1.json covers only Greece, Albania, Bosnia, Bulgaria and Croatia - Cyprus is absent from it, so it was correctly not used.
access_issues: 1) https://www.printecgroup.com/country/printec-cyprus/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to the default fetch tool. RECOVERED by re-requesting the SAME URL over curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent, which returned HTTP 200 and the full page including the live 128-TCR counter and the Bank of Cyprus testimonial. Not dropped. 2) The Bank of Cyprus branch/ATM locator is JavaScript-driven. Its data endpoint was identified by reading /Assets/Scripts/Scripts/storesMap.js as /ajax/StoresPage/GetFilteredStores, which exposes exactly the filters needed (IsATMWithdrawals, IsATMDepositWithdrawals, isCoinDeposit, isCoinDispenser, IsBCS, IsNotesCoins, and the four store-type flags). Six variants were tried - GET and POST, with and without the /en-gb path prefix, with X-Requested-With and Referer headers - and every one returned either a 2-byte empty body or the full page shell with an empty results fragment, so the endpoint appears to require an antiforgery token or a session cookie. LOGGED, not dropped; this is the single highest-value unfinished thread and is raised as an operator request below. 3) https://www.bankofcyprus.com/home-gr/bank_gr/newDepositmachines/ and two sibling URLs surfaced by search return a soft 404 (HTTP 200 with an Error404 page). The live equivalent content was recovered from the Deposit Machines page and the ATM services page instead. 4) All large PDFs were fetched with curl and a desktop User-Agent and parsed locally with pdfminer, in line with the access rule, rather than relying on the fetch tool to render them.
operator_requests: 1) HIGHEST VALUE: drive https://www.bankofcyprus.com/en-gb/Personal/the-bank/storespage/ in a real browser (Claude-in-Chrome or equivalent) with the 'ATM with deposit' filter and then the 'ATM withdrawals only' filter, and record both counts. That yields the deposit-capable share of the c.132 Bank of Cyprus ATMs - the one number that would let the recycler opportunity be sized in units instead of bands. The same locator also filters on Coin Deposit, Coin Dispenser, BCS and Notes & Coins, which would independently validate the 30 / 32 / 5 counts taken from the PDFs. Scripted requests to its /ajax/StoresPage/GetFilteredStores endpoint were refused. 2) Retrieve the full Sesami case study PDF 'Bank of Cyprus: the cash-heavy path towards digitalisation' from the Printec resource library (printecgroup.com resources) - the Printec site 403s the fetch tool and the Sesami web version omits the publication date and the device-model detail. This is the document that would confirm the age profile of the 2018-2021 device vintage. 3) Obtain the Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026 directly rather than through the CBN summary, to confirm the 132 Bank of Cyprus ATM figure and its exact as-at date. NO paywalled sources were encountered - every Bank of Cyprus and Central Bank of Cyprus document used here is free and was successfully retrieved.
